I have farmed this land in the North East for many years, and at eighty I still know what my soil needs. I will apply two small bags of NPK fertilizer to this plot because the land has grown tired, and my beans need some help even though they fix their own nitrogen; I will also spread goat manure as I always do. I keep my own seed from last season because the improved varieties are costly and difficult to find, but I must buy pesticide to fight the pod borers that ruin cowpea if left alone. My sons and grandchildren will provide most of the labor, yet I will hire young men from the village for planting and weeding since I cannot bend like I used to, and we depend on the rains because there is no water for irrigation here.
